title: Normal bundle and zero section
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion with ideal sheaf
$\mathcal I$. The *normal cone* is
$N_{Z/X}=\operatorname{Spec}_Z\bigl(\bigoplus_{r\geq0}\mathcal I^r/ \mathcal I^{r+1}\bigr)$; if $i$ is a
regular immersion of pure
codimension $c$, the conormal sheaf
$\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ is locally free of rank $c$, and
$N_{Z/X}\to Z$ is a *vector bundle* of rank $c$ with a canonical
*zero section* $z:Z\hookrightarrow N_{Z/X}$.

Here the ideal sheaf is that of [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] and its powers are [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. The displayed direct sum is the quasi-coherent graded $\mathcal O_Z$-algebra $\mathcal G$ of [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], so the spectrum is the relative spectrum of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec]. The notation $\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ on $Z$ means the conormal module $\mathcal C=i^*\mathcal I$ [def-pc-module-pullback], not an $\mathcal O_X$-module regarded without change as a sheaf on $Z$. Locally free of rank $c$ is [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], and vector bundle with zero section is [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section]; its zero section here is induced by the projection $\mathcal G\to\mathcal G_0=\mathcal O_Z$.

proof.text: Take the quasi-coherent conormal algebra $\mathcal G$ supplied by [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra]. This supplies its multiplication, its $\mathcal O_Z$-algebra structure, the degree-zero identification with $\mathcal O_Z$, and the degree-one identification with $\mathcal C=i^*\mathcal I$. In particular the direct sum appearing in the definition is a sheaf algebra on $Z$: on $X$ its degree-$n$ pushforward is $\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$, whereas on $Z\cap\operatorname{Spec}R$ it has algebra of sections $\operatorname{gr}_J(R)$ for the defining ideal $J$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](2) to this quasi-coherent algebra and define $N_{Z/X}=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_Z(\mathcal G)$ with its affine projection $p$ to $Z$. The nonnegative grading makes the projection $\epsilon:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G_0=\mathcal O_Z$ multiplicative: the only products with total degree zero have both factors of degree zero. Thus it is an algebra map and is a left inverse of the structural inclusion. The anti-equivalence in clause (3) defines $z:Z\to N_{Z/X}$ and gives $p z=\mathrm{id}_Z$. On any affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $Z$, the inverse image $p^{-1}W=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal G(W)$ is affine, and $z$ is induced by the surjective map $\epsilon_W$, which fixes constants. Since $z^{-1}(p^{-1}W)=W$, these opens cover $N_{Z/X}$ with affine inverse images and surjective structure maps. The converse affine-cover criterion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion](2) proves that $z$ is a closed immersion.

proof.text: Now assume $i$ is regular of pure codimension $c$. The part of [def-pur-regular-immersion] used here is precisely that $X,Z$ are finite type over $k$ and that for each $z\in Z$ the ideal $J_z\subset R_z=\mathcal O_{X,i(z)}$ is generated by an $R_z$-regular sequence of length $c$; the claimed smooth-pair equivalence in that node is not used. The field $k$ is Noetherian, since its ideals are $0$ and $k$, generated by $0$ and $1$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ and $Z$ Noetherian. By [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], $\mathcal C=\mathcal G_1$ is coherent and $\mathcal C_z=J_z/J_z^2$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free] in $R_z$: these stalks are free of rank $c$ over $R_z/J_z=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$. The coherent free-stalk criterion [lem-sc-coherent-free-stalks-locally-free] makes $\mathcal C$ finite locally free. Its local rank is $c$: a rank-$r$ trivialization at $z$ yields $\mathcal C_z\cong\mathcal O_{Z,z}^r$, and reduction modulo the maximal ideal compares vector-space dimensions $r=c$. This proves the exact conormal-rank assertion.

proof.text: Use the canonical graded algebra map $\psi:\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal G$ and its stalk description in [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra]. Fix $z$ and a regular generating sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ of $J_z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free] its classes form a basis of $\mathcal C_z=J_z/J_z^2$. The basis-to-polynomial isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial] identifies $\operatorname{Sym}_{R_z/J_z}(J_z/J_z^2)$ with $(R_z/J_z)[T_1,\ldots,T_c]$, taking the class of $f_j$ to $T_j$ (the isomorphism for a chosen basis follows by the symmetric-algebra universal property, with inverse sending the standard basis back to these classes). Under this identification $\psi_z$ sends $T_j$ to $[f_j]_1$ and fixes constants. It is therefore exactly the map $\theta$ of [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial], which is an isomorphism. This uses all degrees, rather than inferring the associated-graded identification from its degree-one part.

The underlying module map of $\psi$ is bijective on all stalks by Step 4, so [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks] makes it an isomorphism. Its inverse is an algebra map as well: apply $\psi$ to each addition, multiplication, scalar and unit identity for the inverse and use injectivity. Applying the relative-spectrum anti-equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](3) to $\psi:\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal C)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal G$ gives an isomorphism over $Z$ from $N_{Z/X}$ to $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_Z(\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal C))$. Together with the rank-$c$ locally free module of Step 3 this is exactly the vector-bundle data of [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section]. No choice of a globally trivial bundle has been made.

The augmentation of $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal C)$ in [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section] fixes constants and sends every degree-one generator to zero. The composite $\epsilon\psi$ has these same two properties, since $\psi$ preserves degrees and $\epsilon$ is projection to degree zero. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-core] makes these algebra maps equal. Contravariance of the anti-equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](3) says precisely that the isomorphism of Step 5 carries the section $z$ of Step 2 to the vector-bundle zero section. This proves its canonicity and compatibility with the displayed normal-cone construction.
